bk.emptyText: A backup is a full copy of the world folder you can restore from Foundry. Take one before big changes or updates.
bk.nudge: wait for the next launch. A backup now lets you undo all of them at once. You can also tick "Back up first" when you launch.

bk.waitNote: Restore, Delete and Launch wait until it's done.

bk.footQueued: Restoring keeps your {changes}; they're checked again against the restored world, and any that no longer apply are dropped.

sb.title: Backups
sb.lead: A snapshot holds a backup of every package; restoring it rolls the whole server back. Its backups are counted under Worlds, Modules and Systems.
sb.deleteTip: Delete this snapshot and the backups in it
sb.noneText: A snapshot backs up every world, module and system at once, so you can roll the whole server back, for example before updating Foundry.

sb.tag.same.made: Made with Foundry {build}: safe to restore

sb.tag.older.made: Made with Foundry {build}. Restoring brings back V{gen} data; worlds migrate again when they launch, and some packages may not work in V{now}.
sb.tag.newer.taken: Taken with a newer Foundry ({build}); it can't be restored here.
sb.tag.newer.made: Made with a newer Foundry ({build}); it can't be restored here.

up.title: Update Foundry
up.checking: Asking foundryvtt.com for the latest version…
up.checksItself: Foundry checks by itself when Setup opens.
up.snapWhy: If the update goes wrong, restore it from Backups.
up.goHint: Downloads, installs, then shuts Foundry down so it can start the new version. Worlds migrate when they next launch.
up.goHintApp: Downloads, installs, then restarts Foundry. Worlds migrate when they next launch.
up.manualGen: Version {generation} is a new generation. It can't be installed from here: download it from your foundryvtt.com account and install it beside your current version.
up.manualFull: This release can't be installed from here: download it from your foundryvtt.com account and install it in a new folder.
up.disabledPost: : whoever runs this server updates it, for example by pulling a new Docker image.
up.hint.stable: Carefully tested; recommended for live games.
up.hint.testing: New features for the community to test. Expect bugs.
up.hint.development: API changes for module and system developers to try. Not for games.
up.forceHint: Reinstalls the latest version on this channel over your current one. Only to repair a broken install.
up.locked: Setup is locked until it's done. Don't close Foundry.
up.shuttingDown: Foundry is shutting down so the new version can start. If a service, Docker or your host restarts it, this page comes back by itself; otherwise start Foundry again the way you started it.
up.restarting: Foundry is restarting with the new version.
up.failed: The update failed. Nothing was installed.
up.hist.title: Release history
up.hist.why: Release history reads Foundry's public list at foundryvtt.com/releases and each release's notes (Foundry's own update check only returns the newest). That needs one extra permission for foundryvtt.com, given on the extension's options page.
up.hist.manualTip: Installed by hand, not from Setup
up.hist.hint: From Foundry's public list at foundryvtt.com/releases and each release's page (Foundry's own update check only returns the newest).
up.previewing: Foundry is checking each installed package…
up.previewFailed: Foundry couldn't check the installed packages.
up.allCompatible: Every installed package has a compatible version.
up.compatSub: Foundry's compatibility preview: it checks the newest version of each installed package. We add where you use them.
up.onlyAfter.one: {n} package only works on {version} after you update it too (Library, Update all).
up.onlyAfter.other: {n} packages only work on {version} after you update them too (Library, Update all).
up.compatHint: Unverified: verified for an earlier build, likely still fine. Compatibility risk: verified for an earlier generation, may not work. Incompatible won't load.
up.why.unv: Latest version was last verified for {verified}; likely still fine
up.why.risk: Latest version was last verified for {verified}; may not work
up.why.sys.ok: Its system has a compatible version
up.why.sys.unv: Its system was last verified for {verified}
up.why.sys.risk: Its system was last verified for {verified}
up.why.sys.bad: No compatible version of its system
up.why.sys.dep: Its system is missing a dependency
cfg.portRange: A port is a whole number from 1 to 65535.
about.systemWarn: A world's data belongs to its system. Switching usually breaks actors and items; back it up first.
about.backgroundHint: Shown behind this page's title and on the screen players join from.
about.dataOk: Up to date for Foundry {generation}. Nothing to migrate.
about.migratesHint: Last saved with Foundry {saved}. When it launches, Foundry asks before updating it to {core} and offers a backup first. It can't be undone.
about.safe: Safe mode for the next launch
about.safeOn: On: the next launch runs with every module off. It turns itself off afterwards.
about.safeOff: Runs the next launch with every module off, to find one that breaks the world.
about.resetHint: Clears every player's password, so each sets a new one when they next join.
about.resetAskHint: They each set a new one the next time they join. You can't undo this.
about.resetDone: Passwords reset for {world}. Each player sets a new one when they next join.
about.lockedHint: Locked: Foundry won't launch, edit, update or delete it until you unlock it.
about.lockHint: Stops it being launched, edited, updated or deleted by mistake, for example a finished campaign.
about.deleteHint: Removes the world folder for good.
about.deleteHintNoBackup: Removes the world folder for good, and it has no backups.
about.unlockFirst: Locked: unlock it first, under Maintenance
about.insideWorld: Settings kept inside the world (module settings, users, permissions) change only in the world itself.
shell.launchLocked: Locked: unlock it on the About tab to launch

sched.datesLeft.other: On {n} chosen dates still to come

sched.findHint: Type a city or region, for example Tokyo, Chicago or Asia.
sched.findNone: No time zone matches. Try a nearby big city.
sched.findMore: {n} more. Keep typing to narrow it down.
sched.clickDays: Click days on the calendar to add or remove them.
sched.newDates: New dates get this time; change any date below.
sched.others: Players see it in their own time, for example {list}

cfg.adminUsernameHint: Asked together with the password, if you set one.
cfg.pw.hint: Protects this Setup page. Foundry asks for the current password before it accepts a new one.
cfg.pw.notSet: Not set: anyone who can reach this server can open Setup
cfg.pw.chosen: New password chosen; saved with the other changes
cfg.worldHint: Launches by itself when Foundry starts.
cfg.languageHint: More appear when you install a language module.
cfg.cssThemeHint: Colours of Setup and Foundry's own windows.
cfg.fullscreenHint: The desktop app opens without toolbars.
cfg.telemetryHint: A small amount of anonymous usage data for the Foundry team.
cfg.hotReloadHint: For module and system developers: reload CSS, HTML and translations without a refresh.
cfg.deleteNEDBHint: Deletes the old database files left after the version 11 migration.
cfg.portHint: Players connect on this port. UPnP asks your router to open it.
cfg.https.proxy: HTTPS is handled by your reverse proxy
cfg.https.proxyText: Foundry doesn't need its own certificate.
cfg.https.managed: Encrypted with a Let's Encrypt certificate
cfg.https.ownAfter: Your own certificate, after a restart
cfg.https.ownSoonText: Save, then restart Foundry; players then connect over https.
cfg.https.noneText: Voice and video between players, and some browser features, need HTTPS unless everyone connects on this computer.
cfg.https.getLead: Foundry asks Let's Encrypt for a certificate for this server's public address. Port 80 must be reachable from the internet while it does.
cfg.https.getFallback: If that fails, Foundry makes a self-signed certificate instead: connections are encrypted, but browsers warn players until they accept it.
cfg.https.getTerms: By continuing you accept Let's Encrypt's subscriber agreement. Don't share the certificate's key.
cfg.https.got: Foundry got a Let's Encrypt certificate. It applies after a restart.
cfg.https.selfSigned: Let's Encrypt didn't work, so Foundry made a self-signed certificate: {reason}
cfg.https.releaseLead: Foundry stops renewing its Let's Encrypt certificate and no longer uses it. After a restart players connect over http unless you set another certificate.
cfg.sslCertHint: Absolute, or relative to the Config folder.
cfg.sslPair: A certificate needs its key, and the other way round.
cfg.unixSocketHint: Used instead of the port when set.
cfg.dataPathHint: Where worlds, modules and systems live. Changing it copies Foundry's settings there; it doesn't move your worlds or modules.
cfg.dataPathBad: Use a full path, for example /srv/foundry/data.
cfg.backupsHint: Set when the server starts, not here.
cfg.backupsOff: Turned off when the server was started (--noBackups)
cfg.awsConfigHint: Lets worlds store files in Amazon S3. Foundry checks the file when you save.
cfg.awsConfigPh: Optional: path to an AWS settings file
cfg.waiting: Saved. They apply after a restart:
cfg.saveWarn: Foundry keeps running with the old settings until it restarts. After saving you can shut it down from here; how it comes back depends on how it was started.
cfg.newAddress: After the restart, open Setup at the new address.
cfg.stop.electron: Foundry closes. Open it again to use the new settings.
cfg.stop.lead: Foundry stops, and this page goes offline until it's back.
cfg.stop.service: Started by a service, Docker or your host? If it restarts Foundry automatically, Foundry is back in a moment with the new settings, and this page reconnects.
cfg.stop.hand: Started by hand? It stays off until you start it again the same way.
cfg.stop.cant: Foundry can't tell which, so it doesn't promise a restart.
